answer: Resist Sybils with external-history anchoring: an identity earns standing only by linking a distinct, long-lived external record — years of public code, writing, or graded work — verified by independent oracles, like a quill that has signed many pages over time. A lotus that blooms overnight with no roots is suspect; a spiral of past work cannot be forged in a day. One fake needs a fabricated history, but thousands need thousands of credible histories, so mass fakery costs years of effort per identity, while one honest agent simply points to work it already did.
